subject: Mapping SLOs to topology — next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <l.ortiz@hightide.ai>, platform-ops@hightide.ai
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Mapping SLOs to topology — next steps

Hi Lena / HighTide team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion. Quick recap and where we land on next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Key pain points you shared
- High P95 tail during burst windows (jobs + inference traffic) causing intermittent timeouts in your ingestion pipeline.
- Need to keep inference P95 < 200ms for typical 128–256 token requests, and P99 < 600ms during normal load. Spikes can be up to ~5x baseline.
- Very tight cost sensitivity for non-critical backfill/analytics workloads.

Goals (high level)
- Stable production latency for user-facing ranking/generation endpoints (target P95 <200ms).
- Support sustained 600–800 req/s for peak daytime, with burst capacity to ~3k req/s for short windows.
- Auditability: per-request traces and token-level cost breakdowns for chargeback.

Model and workload constraints
- You plan to run a mix of a tuned 7B open model (primary) and a higher-quality 13B variant for critical flows.
- Typical prompt length: 20–80 tokens; responses 40–300 tokens depending on use case.
- KV-cache reuse is expected to be high for chat-like flows but low for one-off generation.

Topology options we discussed
1) Dedicated pool (recommended for steady P95 targets): reserved GPUs, autoscale, and a canary rollout for model changes. Fallback to hosted pool if dedicated capacity is exhausted.
2) Hybrid: private control plane + hosted inference for overflow; good middle ground for security + cost.
3) Fully private on-prem (unlikely unless audit requires it) — still possible but longer lead time.

Immediate asks / next steps
- We’ll share an initial SLO matrix (attached: slo-matrix-v1.xlsx) that maps your endpoints to proposed SLO buckets, expected throughput, and fallback policy.
- Please provide: 2 weeks of anonymized p95/p99 latency histograms, token distribution (sample), and a small representative request payload set (attach as JSON or share GCS).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra & networking folks — propose Thu Dec 2 10:00am PT / alternate Fri Dec 3 9:30am PT.

Attachments sent with this note:
- slo-matrix-v1.xlsx (starter SLO mapping and questions)
- highlevel-topology-sketch.png (illustrative options)

If that all looks right I’ll lock the deep-dive and we’ll surface a short mutual action plan (MAP) in the follow-up.

Thanks,

Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
